items.title: 52115_Danny Barker oral history interview
items.q: This guy in Newark... It was Mohammed.

ctx.x: Yeah, from Detroit. He was out at this... Well, he was with me. He said, 'Man, what are you talkin' about? You gotta play this music.' He said, 'I ain't playin' no more Blues.' He said, 'Well, lay out.' So he sat there. And he started hanging out. He'd met some musicians from New York that was there, Louis Metcalf and them, and they wanted him, because he was playing modern -- he was a bopper. But he was starving to death, you know, in New York, because the Boppers weren't working too much. There was a few of the…
Yeah, Mosque Clubs they called them.
